1) direct optogenetic activation of mossy fibers of the MCP can serve as an efficient CS replacement for both the DEC and the trace classical eyeblink-conditioning (TEC) learning, and 2) the cerebellum can independently modulate both DEC, and TET with a trace interval up to 350 ms.
the cerebellar circuitry is able to independently support both delay and trace eyeblink conditioning with trace intervals of 150 or of 350 ms.
the cerebellar circuitry can support both the simple delay eyeblink conditioning and the trace eyeblink conditioning with short trace intervals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ability of the isolated cerebellum to support associative learning and the cerebellar circuitry involved in associative learning.
the ability of the mammalian cerebellum to support both simple and complex associative motor learning.
the ability of the isolated cerebellum to independently modulate associative motor learning with a shorter trace intervals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cerebellar system is sufficient to independently support associative motor learning with a trace interval as long as 350 ms.
the cerebellar system is sufficient for the acquisition of DEC, and TES with a trace interval up to 350 ms.
the cerebellar system is a sufficient neuronal system to support the DEC, and to support the TEC with trace intervals of 150 or even 350 ms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cerebellar circuitry is sufficient to independently support both delay and trace associative learning with short trace intervals, but not long trace intervals.

the cerebellar system is sufficient for simple associative motor learning and for more complex associative motor learning with shorter trace intervals, but not for more complex associative learning with a trace interval over a certain limit.

the cerebellar circuitry is sufficient and essential to support the associative motor learning and that the cerebellums ability to independently learn the TEC is limited to the trace interval of 350 ms or less.

the cerebellar circuitry can learn and store the simple DEC, but not the more complex TEC with a longer trace interval.
